units.zh: 梁書卷第三十七 列傳第三十一
units.en: Book of Liang, Volume 37, Biography 31
units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 37, Biography 31

units.zh: 謝舉 何敬容
units.en: Xie Ju; He Jingrong
units.literal: Xie Ju; He Jingrong

units.zh: 謝舉，字言揚，中書令覽之弟也。
units.en: Xie Ju, whose courtesy name was Yanyang, was the younger brother of Xie Lan, Director of the Palace Secretariat.
units.literal: Xie Ju, courtesy name Yanyang, was the younger brother of Zhongshu Ling Xie Lan.

units.zh: 幼好學，能清言，與覽齊名。
units.en: As a boy he loved study, excelled at pure conversation, and was as famous as his brother Lan.
units.literal: From youth he loved learning and could engage in pure conversation; he was as renowned as Lan.

units.zh: 舉年十四，嘗贈沈約五言詩，爲約稱賞。
units.en: When Ju was fourteen he once gave Shen Yue a pentasyllabic poem, and Yue praised it highly.
units.literal: At fourteen Ju once presented Shen Yue with a pentasyllabic poem, which Yue praised.

units.zh: 世人爲之語曰：「王有養、炬，謝有覽、舉。」
units.en: People said of them: “The Wangs have Yang and Ju; the Xies have Lan and Ju.”
units.literal: People said of them: “The Wangs have Yang and Ju; the Xies have Lan and Ju.”

units.zh: 養、炬，王筠、王泰小字也。
units.en: Yang and Ju were the childhood names of Wang Jun and Wang Tai.
units.literal: Yang and Ju were the childhood names of Wang Jun and Wang Tai.

units.zh: 起家秘書郎，遷太子舍人，輕車功曹史，秘書丞，司空從事中郎，太子庶子，家令，掌東宮管記，深爲昭明太子賞接。
units.en: He entered service as a Secretariat gentleman, then rose through posts as heir-apparent attendant, merit-office secretary, secretariat aide, masters-of-works attendant, crown-prince household administrator, and household master, overseeing the Eastern Palace archives, and won the deep favor of Crown Prince Zhaoming.
units.literal: He began his career as Secretary Gentleman, was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, Secretary Gentleman of the Light Chariot Merit Office, Secretariat Assistant, Attendant Gentleman of the Masters of Works, Crown Prince’s Household Administrator, and Household Master; he managed the Eastern Palace record office and was deeply favored by Crown Prince Zhaoming.

units.zh: 秘書監任昉出爲新安郡，別舉詩云：「詎念耋嗟人，方深老夫託。」
units.en: When Ren Fang, Director of the Secretariat, left for Xin’an Commandery, he sent Ju a farewell poem: “I would not dwell on the groaning elder—yet how deeply I place my trust in you, old friend.”
units.literal: When Secretariat Director Ren Fang went out to Xin’an Commandery, he parted with a poem to Ju saying: “How could I think of the sighing old man—yet how deeply I entrust myself to you, my elder friend.”

units.zh: 其屬意如此。
units.en: Such was the feeling he meant to convey.
units.literal: His intent was of this sort.

units.zh: 嘗侍宴華林園，高祖訪舉於覽，覽對曰：「識藝過臣甚遠，惟飲酒不及於臣。」
units.en: Once at a banquet in Huaglin Garden the Founding Emperor asked Lan about Ju; Lan answered: “His learning and skill far exceed mine—only in wine he cannot match me.”
units.literal: Once while attending a banquet in Huaglin Garden, the Founding Emperor inquired about Ju through Lan; Lan replied: “His knowledge and talent far surpass mine; only in drinking he does not equal me.”

units.zh: 高祖大悅。
units.en: The Founding Emperor was delighted.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 轉太子中庶子，猶掌管記。
units.en: He was made an attendant in the heir’s palace while continuing to keep the archives.
units.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Crown Prince’s Palace, still managing the records.

units.zh: 天監十一年，遷侍中。
units.en: In Tianjian 11, Ju was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
units.literal: In Tianjian 11, Ju was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 十四年，出爲寧遠將軍、豫章內史，爲政和理，甚得民心。
units.en: In the fourteenth year, he went out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and Interior Minister of Yuzhang. His governance was harmonious and orderly, and he greatly won the hearts of the people.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year, he went out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and Interior Minister of Yuzhang. His governance was harmonious and orderly, and he greatly won the hearts of the people.

units.zh: 十八年，復入爲侍中，領步兵校尉。
units.en: In the eighteenth year, he again entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Infantry Colonel.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year, he again entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Infantry Colonel.

units.zh: 普通元年，出爲貞毅將軍、太尉臨川王長史。
units.en: In Putong 1, he went out as General of Firm Resoluteness and chief clerk to the Prince of Linchuan, Grand Commandant.
units.literal: In Putong 1, he went out as General of Firm Resoluteness and chief clerk to the Prince of Linchuan, Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 四年，入爲左民尚書。
units.en: In the fourth year, he entered court as Minister of the Left People.
units.literal: In the fourth year, he entered court as Minister of the Left People.

units.zh: 其年遷掌吏部，尋以公事免。
units.en: That year he was transferred to administer the Ministry of Personnel, but soon was dismissed over an official matter.
units.literal: That year he was transferred to administer the Ministry of Personnel, but soon was dismissed over an official matter.

units.zh: 五年，起爲太子中庶子，領右軍將軍。
units.en: In the fifth year, he was recalled as Household Attendant to the Crown Prince, concurrently General of the Right Army.
units.literal: In the fifth year, he was recalled as Household Attendant to the Crown Prince, concurrently General of the Right Army.

units.zh: 六年，復爲左民尚書，領步兵校尉。
units.en: In the sixth year, he again became Minister of the Left People, concurrently Infantry Colonel.
units.literal: In the sixth year, he again became Minister of the Left People, concurrently Infantry Colonel.

units.zh: 俄徙爲吏部尚書，尋加侍中。
units.en: Soon he was shifted to Minister of Personnel, and before long was additionally Attendant-in-Ordinary.
units.literal: Soon he was shifted to Minister of Personnel, and before long was additionally Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 出爲仁威將軍、晉陵太守。
units.en: He went out as General of Benevolent Awe and administrator of Jinling.
units.literal: He went out as General of Benevolent Awe and administrator of Jinling.

units.zh: 在郡清靜，百姓化其德，境內肅然。
units.en: In the commandery he was clear and tranquil; the common people were transformed by his virtue, and the territory was orderly and respectful.
units.literal: In the commandery he was clear and tranquil; the common people were transformed by his virtue, and the territory was orderly and respectful.

units.zh: 罷郡還，吏民詣闕請立碑，詔許之。
units.en: When he left the commandery and returned to court, the officials and people went to the palace gate to request permission to erect a stele, and an edict allowed it.
units.literal: When he left the commandery and returned to court, the officials and people went to the palace gate to request permission to erect a stele, and an edict allowed it.

units.zh: 大通二年，入爲侍中、五兵尚書，未拜，遷掌吏部，侍中如故。
units.en: In Datong 2, he entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of the Five Armies, but before taking office was transferred to administer the Ministry of Personnel, remaining Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
units.literal: In Datong 2, he entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of the Five Armies, but before taking office was transferred to administer the Ministry of Personnel, remaining Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.

units.zh: 舉祖莊，宋世再典選，至舉又三爲此職，前代未有也。
units.en: Ju's grandfather Zhuang had twice managed personnel selection in the Song period; down to Ju, who held this office three more times, there had been no such precedent in earlier ages.
units.literal: Ju's grandfather Zhuang had twice managed personnel selection in the Song period; down to Ju, who held this office three more times, there had been no such precedent in earlier ages.

units.zh: 舉少博涉多通，尤長玄理及釋氏義。
units.en: In his youth Ju read widely and mastered many fields, above all metaphysics and Buddhist teaching.
units.literal: Ju in his youth was broadly learned in many subjects and especially excelled in arcane learning and Buddhist doctrine.

units.zh: 爲晉陵郡時，常與義僧遞講經論，徵士何胤自虎丘山赴之。
units.en: As governor of Jinling he often exchanged lectures on scripture and doctrine with Buddhist monks, and the recluse He Yin would come from Tiger Hill to hear them.
units.literal: While he was governor of Jinling Commandery he often lectured in turn on sutras and treatises with Buddhist monks, and the recluse He Yin came from Tiger Hill to join them.

units.zh: 其盛如此。
units.en: The assemblies were as grand as that.
units.literal: Such was the flourishing of these gatherings.

units.zh: 先是，北渡人盧廣有儒術，爲國子博士，于學發講，僕射徐勉以下畢至。
units.en: Earlier the northern scholar Lu Guang, skilled in Confucian learning, was Erudite of the National University; when he lectured there, Vice Director Xu Mian and the rest all attended.
units.literal: Before this, the northerner Lu Guang had mastery of Confucian learning and was National University Libationer; he opened lectures at the university and all the vice directors including Xu Mian came.

units.zh: 舉造坐，屢折廣，辭理通邁。
units.en: Ju took a seat and repeatedly overturned Guang’s points, his argument lucid and bold.
units.literal: Ju went to take a seat and repeatedly refuted Guang; his reasoning was penetrating and far-reaching.

units.zh: 廣深嘆服，仍以所執麈尾薦之，以況重席焉。
units.en: Guang marveled and, in token of esteem, gave Ju the fly-whisk in his hand—as if setting out a second mat for a master.
units.literal: Guang sighed deeply in admiration and moreover offered Ju the fly-whisk he held, comparing him to one honored with a second mat.

units.zh: 四年，加侍中。
units.en: In the fourth year he was made Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 五年，遷尚書右僕射，侍中如故。
units.en: In the fifth year he became Right Vice Director of the Secretariat while retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, his status as Palace Attendant remaining.

units.zh: 大同三年，以疾陳解，徙爲右光祿大夫，給親信二十人。
units.en: In the third year of Datong he asked leave on grounds of illness and was shifted to Right Master of the Imperial Household with twenty personal attendants.
units.literal: In the third year of Datong he submitted a petition citing illness to resign and was moved to Right Household Master of the Imperial Household, with twenty personal attendants granted.

units.zh: 其年，出爲雲麾將軍、吳郡太守。
units.en: That same year he left the capital as Cloud-Banner General and Governor of Wu.
units.literal: That year he went out as Cloud-Banner General and Governor of Wu Commandery.

units.zh: 先是，何敬容居郡有美績，世稱爲何吳郡。
units.en: Earlier, when He Jingrong had governed the commandery, his record was so fine that men called him “He of Wu Commandery.”
units.literal: Before this, He Jingrong when governing the commandery had excellent achievements and was known to the age as “He of Wu Commandery.”

units.zh: 及舉爲政，聲跡略相比。
units.en: Under Ju’s rule his reputation and deeds were nearly on a par.
units.literal: When Ju took over the administration, his reputation and conduct were on the whole comparable.

units.zh: 六年，入爲侍中、中書監，未拜，遷太子詹事、翊左將軍，侍中如故。
units.en: In the sixth year he returned as Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat; before he could assume the latter post he was made Grand Warden of the Heir Apparent and General of the Left Guards, still Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In the sixth year he entered court as Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Library; before he took the seal he was transferred to Grand Warden of the Heir Apparent and General of the Left Guards, his status as Palace Attendant unchanged.

units.zh: 舉父瀹，齊世終此官，累表乞改授，敕不許，久之方就職。
units.en: Ju’s father Yue had ended his career in that same office under Qi; Ju memorialized again and again to be given a different post, but the throne refused until, after long delay, he at last entered upon the duty.
units.literal: Ju’s father Xie Yue in Qi times had ended his career in this very office, and Ju repeatedly submitted memorials begging to resign and receive another appointment, but the edict did not permit it; only after a long time did he finally take up the post.

units.zh: 九年，遷尚書僕射，侍中、將軍如故。
units.en: In the ninth year he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, retaining Palace Attendant and general’s rank.
units.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, his posts as Palace Attendant and General remaining.

units.zh: 舉雖居端揆，未嘗肯預時務，多因疾陳解。
units.en: Though he stood at the head of government, Ju never cared to meddle in the day’s business and often pleaded illness to withdraw.
units.literal: Although Ju occupied the highest counsellor’s seat he had never been willing to involve himself in current affairs, and many times cited illness in petitions to resign.

units.zh: 敕輒賜假，並手敕處方，加給上藥。
units.en: Each time the emperor granted him leave, wrote prescriptions in his own hand, and sent the finest drugs.
units.literal: The emperor would each time grant him leave and with his own hand write prescriptions, adding superior medicines.

units.zh: 其恩遇如此。
units.en: Such was the grace shown him.
units.literal: His favor was of this sort.

units.zh: 其年，以本官參掌選事。
units.en: That year he also took part in appointments in his existing rank.
units.literal: That year he participated in selection affairs in his existing office.

units.zh: 太清二年，遷尚書令，侍中、將軍如故。
units.en: In the second year of Taiqing he became Director of the Secretariat, still Palace Attendant and general.
units.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, remaining Palace Attendant and General.

units.zh: 是歲，侯景寇京師，舉卒于圍內。
units.en: That year, when Hou Jing besieged the capital, Ju died inside the encircled city.
units.literal: That year, when Hou Jing attacked the capital, Ju died within the siege.

units.zh: 詔贈侍中、中衛將軍、開府儀同三司，侍中、尚書令如故。
units.en: An edict mourned him with Palace Attendant, Central Guard General, and Grand Honorific with the Three Insignia, while his posts as Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat stood unchanged.
units.literal: The edict posthumously awarded him Palace Attendant, Central Guard General, and Grand Honorific with the Three Insignia, his offices of Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat remaining.

units.zh: 文集亂中並亡逸。
units.en: His collected works perished entirely in the upheaval.
units.literal: His collected writings were all lost in the disorders.

units.zh: 二子禧，嘏，並少知名。
units.en: His two sons Xi and Gu were both noted while young.
units.literal: His two sons Xi and Gu were both known in youth.

units.zh: 嘏，太清中，歷太子中庶子，出爲建安太守。
units.en: Gu, in the Taiqing era, served as heir’s attendant and then went out as Administrator of Jian’an.
units.literal: Gu during Taiqing rose through Crown Prince’s Attendant and went out as Administrator of Jian’an.

units.zh: 何敬容，字國禮，廬江人也。
units.en: He Jingrong, courtesy name Guoli, came from Lujiang.
units.literal: He Jingrong, courtesy name Guoli, was a man of Lujiang.

units.zh: 祖攸之，宋太常卿；
units.en: His grandfather Youzhi had been Grand Minister of Ceremonies under Song;
units.literal: His grandfather Youzhi was Grand Minister of Ceremonies in Song;

units.zh: 父昌珝，齊吏部尚書；
units.en: his father Changxu had been Director of the Imperial Secretariat under Qi;
units.literal: his father Changxu was Director of the Imperial Secretariat in Qi;

units.zh: 並有名前代。
units.en: both were celebrated in earlier ages.
units.literal: both enjoyed fame in previous dynasties.

units.zh: 敬容以名家子，弱冠選尚齊武帝女長城公主，拜駙馬都尉。
units.en: Jingrong, as the son of a distinguished house, was selected in his early twenties to marry Emperor Wu of Qi's daughter, Princess Changcheng, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.
units.literal: Jingrong, as the son of a distinguished house, was selected in his early twenties to marry Emperor Wu of Qi's daughter, Princess Changcheng, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.

units.zh: 天監初，爲秘書郎，歷太子舍人，尚書殿中郎，太子洗馬，中書舍人，秘書丞，遷揚州治中。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianjian he became Palace Library Gentleman, and then served successively as crown prince attendant, Palace Gentleman in the Department of State Affairs, Groom of the Crown Prince, Secretariat Drafter, and Assistant Director of the Palace Library, before being transferred to administrative aide of Yangzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he became Palace Library Gentleman, and then served successively as crown prince attendant, Palace Gentleman in the Department of State Affairs, Groom of the Crown Prince, Secretariat Drafter, and Assistant Director of the Palace Library, before being transferred to administrative aide of Yangzhou.

units.zh: 出爲建安內史，清公有美績，民吏稱之。
units.en: He went out as Interior Minister of Jian'an, where he was honest and fair and achieved an excellent record, and the people and officials praised him.
units.literal: He went out as Interior Minister of Jian'an, where he was honest and fair and achieved an excellent record, and the people and officials praised him.

units.zh: 還除黃門郎，累遷太子中庶子，散騎常侍，侍中，司徒左長史。
units.en: On returning to court he was appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman, then rose successively to Junior Mentor in the heir apparent's household, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and left chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.
units.literal: On returning to court he was appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman, then rose successively to Household Attendant to the Crown Prince, Regular Attendant, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and left chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.

units.zh: 普通二年，復爲侍中，領羽林監，俄又領本州大中正。
units.en: In the second year of Putong, he again became Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Director of the Feathered Forest Guard, and soon also served as Grand Rectifier of his home province.
units.literal: In Putong 2, he again became Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently director of the Feathered Forest Guard, and soon also served as grand rectifier of his home province.

units.zh: 頃之，守吏部尚書，銓序明審，號爲稱職。
units.en: Before long, he acted as Minister of Personnel; his selection and ordering of officials were clear and careful, and he was considered competent in the post.
units.literal: Before long, he acted as Minister of Personnel; his selection and ordering of officials were clear and careful, and he was considered competent in the post.

units.zh: 四年，出爲招遠將軍、吳郡太守，爲政勤恤民隱，辨訟如神，視事四年，治爲天下第一。
units.en: In the fourth year, he went out as General Who Summons the Distant and administrator of Wu Commandery. In governing he diligently cared for the people's hardships and judged lawsuits with almost uncanny precision. After four years in office, his administration was ranked first in the realm.
units.literal: In the fourth year, he went out as General Who Summons the Distant and administrator of Wu Commandery. In governing he diligently cared for the people's hardships and judged lawsuits with almost uncanny precision. After four years in office, his administration was ranked first in the realm.

units.zh: 吏民詣闕請樹碑，詔許之。
units.en: The officials and people went to the palace gate to request permission to erect a stele, and an edict allowed it.
units.literal: The officials and people went to the palace gate to request permission to erect a stele, and an edict allowed it.

units.zh: 大通二年，徵爲中書令，未拜，復爲吏部尚書，領右軍將軍，俄加侍中。
units.en: In Datong 2, he was summoned as Secretariat Director, but before taking office he was again made Minister of Personnel, concurrently General of the Right Army, and soon additionally Attendant-in-Ordinary.
units.literal: In Datong 2, he was summoned as Secretariat Director, but before taking office he was again made Minister of Personnel, concurrently General of the Right Army, and soon additionally Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 中大通元年，改太子中庶子。
units.en: In Zhongdatong 1, he was changed to Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.
units.literal: In Zhongdatong 1, he was changed to Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.

units.zh: 敬容身長八尺，白皙美鬚眉。
units.en: Jingrong stood eight chi tall, with fair skin and handsome beard and brows.
units.literal: Jingrong’s stature was eight chi; he was fair-skinned with handsome beard and brows.

units.zh: 性矜莊，衣冠尤事鮮麗，每公庭就列，容止出人。
units.en: Proud and formal by nature, he lavished care on bright, elegant dress; whenever he took his place at court his bearing outshone the rest.
units.literal: His nature was proud and dignified; above all he paid attention to fresh and beautiful dress, and whenever he took his place in public assembly his bearing exceeded other men.

units.zh: 三年，遷尚書右僕射，參掌選事，侍中如故。
units.en: In the third year he became Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and shared in appointments, still Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and participated in selection affairs, his status as Palace Attendant remaining.

units.zh: 時僕射徐勉參掌機密，以疾陳解，因舉敬容自代，故有此授焉。
units.en: Vice Director Xu Mian then held the secret reins of power; when he resigned on grounds of illness he recommended Jingrong to succeed him, and so the post fell to him.
units.literal: At the time Vice Director Xu Mian managed secret affairs; citing illness he resigned, and therefore nominated Jingrong to replace him—hence this appointment.

units.zh: 五年，遷左僕射，加宣惠將軍，置佐史，侍中、參掌如故。
units.en: In the fifth year he was made Left Vice Director and General Who Spreads Grace, with clerks assigned, while he remained Palace Attendant and kept his role in administration.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Left Vice Director, with the added title of General Who Spreads Grace, staff clerks appointed, his status as Palace Attendant and participation in management remaining.

units.zh: 大同三年正月，朱雀門災，高祖謂羣臣曰：「此門制卑狹，我始欲構，遂遭天火。」
units.en: In the first month of the third year of Datong the Vermilion Bird Gate burned; the Founding Emperor told the ministers: “The gate was built too low and cramped—I had only just meant to rebuild it when Heaven sent this blaze.”
units.literal: In the first month of the third year of Datong, the Vermilion Bird Gate caught fire; the Founding Emperor said to the assembled ministers: “This gate was made low and narrow; I had just intended to rebuild it when Heaven sent this fire.”

units.zh: 並相顧未有答。
units.en: The courtiers looked at one another and none answered.
units.literal: They all looked at one another without any reply.

units.zh: 敬容獨曰：「此所謂陛下『先天而天不違』。」
units.en: Only Jingrong spoke: “This is what Your Majesty calls acting before Heaven so that Heaven does not oppose you.”
units.literal: Jingrong alone said: “This is what Your Majesty means when you ‘act before Heaven, and Heaven does not contradict you.’”

units.zh: 時以爲名對。
units.en: Men at the time hailed it as a brilliant reply.
units.literal: The time regarded this as a celebrated retort.

units.zh: 俄遷中權將軍、丹陽尹，侍中、參掌、佐史如故。
units.en: Soon he was made Central Authority General and Intendant of Danyang, keeping Palace Attendant, his administrative role, and his staff.
units.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Central Authority General and Intendant of Danyang, his status as Palace Attendant, participation in affairs, and staff clerks remaining.

units.zh: 五年，入爲尚書令，侍中、將軍、參掌、佐史如故。
units.en: In the fifth year he returned as Director of the Secretariat, still Palace Attendant, general, administrator, and chief clerk.
units.literal: In the fifth year he entered court as Director of the Secretariat, his status as Palace Attendant, General, participation in affairs, and staff clerks remaining.

units.zh: 敬容久處臺閣，詳悉舊事，且聰明識治，勤於簿領，詰朝理事，日旰不休。
units.en: Long in the secretariat, Jingrong knew every old rule by heart; clever and skilled in affairs, he toiled over registers and papers, taking up business at dawn and working past sunset without pause.
units.literal: Jingrong had long been in the secretariat and knew the old precedents in detail; moreover he was intelligent and understood governance, diligent over ledgers and documents, examining court business each morning until sundown without rest.

units.zh: 自晉、宋以來，宰相皆文義自逸，敬容獨勤庶務，爲世所嗤鄙。
units.en: From Jin and Song onward ministers had prided themselves on literary ease; Jingrong alone sweated over clerical work, and the age sneered at him.
units.literal: Since Jin and Song, chancellors had all found leisure in literary elegance; Jingrong alone toiled over routine matters and was scoffed at by the age.

units.zh: 時蕭琛子巡者，頗有輕薄才，因制卦名離合等詩以嘲之，敬容處之如初，亦不屑也。
units.en: Xiao Chen’s son Xun had a gift for light verse and wrote riddling poems from hexagram names to ridicule him; Jingrong bore it as before and would not stoop to reply.
units.literal: At the time Xun, son of Xiao Chen, had rather frivolous talent and therefore composed poems with hexagram-name word-splitting and the like to mock him; Jingrong treated him as before and did not deign to notice.

units.zh: 十一年，坐妾弟費慧明爲導倉丞，夜盜官米，爲禁司所執，送領軍府。
units.en: In the eleventh year his concubine’s younger brother Fei Huiming, a grain-depot clerk, stole government grain by night; the patrol seized him and handed him to the Rear Guard command.
units.literal: In the eleventh year his concubine’s younger brother Fei Huiming served as grain depot clerk; at night he stole official grain, was seized by the prohibition officers, and sent to the Army of the Rear Guard headquarters.

units.zh: 時河東王譽爲領軍將軍，敬容以書解慧明，譽即封書以奏。
units.en: Prince of Hedong Xiao Yu then commanded the Rear Guard; Jingrong wrote to plead for Huiming, and Yu at once sealed the letter and reported it to the throne.
units.literal: At the time Prince of Hedong Yu was General of the Rear Guard; Jingrong wrote a letter interceding for Huiming, and Yu immediately sealed the letter and memorialized it.

units.zh: 高祖大怒，付南司推劾。
units.en: The Founding Emperor was enraged and sent the case to the Southern Office for prosecution.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor was furious and handed him over to the Southern Office for investigation.

units.zh: 御史中丞張綰奏敬容挾私罔上，合棄市刑，詔特免職。
units.en: Censor Zhang Wan charged that Jingrong had used private ties to mislead the throne and deserved death; an edict spared his life but stripped him of office.
units.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Zan memorialized that Jingrong practiced favoritism and deceived his sovereign, deserving execution; the edict specially exempted him only from office.

units.zh: 初，天監中，有沙門釋寶志者，嘗遇敬容，謂曰：「君後必貴，然終是何敗何耳」。
units.en: Earlier, in the Tianjian era, the monk Baozhi had met him and said: “You are sure to reach the heights, yet in the end—what defeat, what?”
units.literal: Earlier in the Tianjian era the monk Baozhi had once met Jingrong and said: “You will certainly rise to eminence, yet in the end—what defeat, what?”

units.zh: 及敬容爲宰相，謂何姓當爲其禍，故抑沒宗族，無仕進者，至是竟爲河東所敗。
units.en: Once he was chancellor he feared harm from anyone surnamed He and blocked his clan from office; in the end he was brought down by the Prince of Hedong.
units.literal: When Jingrong became chancellor he thought the He surname would be his calamity, so he suppressed his clan and none obtained advancement; in the end he was indeed ruined by Hedong.

units.zh: 中大同元年三月，高祖幸同泰寺講《金字三慧經》，敬容請預聽，敕許之。
units.en: In the third month of the first year of Zhongdatong the Founding Emperor went to Tongtai Temple to expound the Golden-character Three Wisdom Sutra; Jingrong asked to hear it and was allowed by edict.
units.literal: In the third month of the first year of Zhongdatong, the Founding Emperor visited Tongtai Temple to lecture on the Golden-character Three Wisdom Sutra; Jingrong asked to attend and was permitted by edict.

units.zh: 又有敕聽朔望問訊。
units.en: Another edict let him attend the new- and full-moon audiences to offer greetings.
units.literal: There was also an edict allowing him to pay court on the new and full moon for ritual inquiries.

units.zh: 尋起爲金紫光祿大夫，未拜，又加侍中。
units.en: Soon he was recalled as Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; before he could accept it he was again made Palace Attendant.
units.literal: Before long he was restored as Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; before he accepted the seal he was again promoted to Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 敬容舊時賓客門生喧嘩如昔，冀其復用。
units.en: His old clients and students raised the same clamor as before, hoping he would be used again.
units.literal: Jingrong’s former clients and disciples made as loud a commotion as of old, hoping he would be reemployed.

units.zh: 會稽謝鬱致書戒之曰：「草萊之人，聞諸道路，君侯已得瞻望朝夕，出入禁門，醉尉將不敢呵，灰然不無其漸，甚休，甚休！
units.en: Xie Yu of Kuaiji wrote to warn him: “From common report we hear that you may once more gaze on the court at dawn and dusk and pass the palace gates—that even the drunken gate guard will not bark at you—yet the slope is not absent; how fortunate, how fortunate!
units.literal: Xie Yu of Kuaiji sent him a letter of admonition saying: “A man of the fields, hearing talk on the road, learns that you may again look upon the court morning and evening, pass in and out of the forbidden gates, and that the drunken gatekeeper will not dare to shout you down—yet there is no lack of a gradual slide; most fortunate, most fortunate!

units.zh: 敢賀於前，又將吊也。
units.en: I congratulate you beforehand—and I must mourn you as well.
units.literal: I venture congratulations in advance, yet I must also offer condolences.

units.zh: 昔流言裁作，公旦東奔；
units.en: When rumor first arose, the Duke of Zhou fled east;
units.literal: In olden days when slander spread, the Duke of Zhou fled east;

units.zh: 燕書始來，子孟不入。
units.en: when the letter from Yan came, Zi Meng would not go in.
units.literal: when the Yan letter first arrived, Zi Meng would not enter.

units.zh: 夫聖賢被虛過以自斥，未有嬰時釁而求親者也。
units.en: Sages have been slandered and therefore held themselves back; no wise man has ever sought intimacy at a time of blame.
units.literal: Sages and worthies have been reproached on false charges and therefore restrained themselves; never has one courted favor at a moment of scandal.

units.zh: 且曝鰓之鱗，不念杯杓之水；
units.en: Fish with drying gills do not think of a cup of water;
units.literal: Moreover, fish with gills laid bare do not think of a cup of water;

units.zh: 雲霄之翼，豈顧籠樊之糧。
units.en: wings that touch the clouds do not glance at fodder in a pen.
units.literal: wings that reach the clouds do not look back at grain in a cage.

units.zh: 何者？
units.en: Why?
units.literal: Why?

units.zh: 所托已盛也。
units.en: Because what they rest on is already vast.
units.literal: What they rely on is already great.

units.zh: 昔君侯納言加首，鳴玉在腰，回豊貂以步文昌，聳高蟬而趨武帳，可謂盛矣。
units.en: Once, when you were chief minister, jade chimed at your belt; you swept sable robes as you entered Wenchang and lifted your cicada crest as you hastened to the martial hall—truly a time of glory.
units.literal: In former days when you were chief counsellor, jade tinkled at your waist; you turned rich sable as you walked to Wenchang and raised high your cicada hat as you hurried to the military hall—one might call that splendor indeed.

units.zh: 不以此時薦才拔士，少報聖主之恩；
units.en: You did not then lift men of talent to repay your sovereign’s kindness;
units.literal: You did not then recommend talent and advance scholars to repay the sage ruler’s grace;

units.zh: 今卒如爰絲之說，受責見過，方復欲更窺朝廷，觖望萬分，竊不爲左右取也。
units.en: now, as Master Ai’s words have it, you bear blame and fault, yet you would look again toward the court and hope for the slightest chance—I cannot think this wise for you.
units.literal: now at last, as Master Ai’s saying goes, you are blamed and found at fault, yet you would again peer into court and hope for a ten-thousandth chance—I do not think this wise for you.

units.zh: 昔竇嬰、楊惲亦得罪明時，不能謝絕賓客，猶交黨援，卒無後福，終益前禍。
units.en: Dou Ying and Yang Yun too offended a luminous court; unable to shut their doors to guests, they still traded on connections, and in the end won no blessing but deepened their fall.
units.literal: In olden days Dou Ying and Yang Yun also fell from favor in a bright age; they could not cut off their clients and still kept up factional ties, and in the end found no lasting blessing but only added to their former disaster.

units.zh: 僕之所吊，實在於斯。
units.en: My condolences are for this very thing.
units.literal: What I mourn is precisely this.

units.zh: 人人所以頗猶有踵君侯之門者，未必皆感惠懷仁，有灌夫、任安之義，乃戒翟公之大署，冀君侯之復用也。
units.en: Those who still throng your door are not all moved by grace or bound like Guan Fu and Ren An; they dread Duke Zhai’s famous notice and hope for your return to power.
units.literal: The reason men still somewhat crowd your gate is not necessarily that they feel your kindness or owe you the loyalty of Guan Fu or Ren An; they fear Duke Zhai’s great inscription and hope you will be used again.

units.zh: 夫在思過之日，而挾復用之意，未可爲智者說矣。
units.en: To cling to hope of office while you should be repenting is not counsel fit for a wise man.
units.literal: To harbor hope of reuse on a day meant for reflection on faults is not something one can explain to the wise.

units.zh: 君侯宜杜門念失，無有所通，築茅茨于鐘阜，聊優遊以卒歲，見可憐之意，著待終之情。
units.en: Shut your door, ponder your fault, deal with no one, raise a thatched hut on Bell Peak, and live out your days at leisure, showing that you accept reproach and await your end.
units.literal: You ought to shut your door and dwell on your error, have no dealings with others, build a thatched hut on Bell Mountain, and pass your remaining years in ease, showing a mind open to pity and a spirit ready for the end.

units.zh: 復仲尼能改之言，惟子貢更也之譬，少戢言於衆口，微自救於竹帛，所謂『失之東隅，收之桑榆』。
units.en: Remember that Confucius said a man may mend his ways, and Zigong that one may change; speak less to the multitude and rescue yourself a little on the page—that is “what is lost at sunrise is gained at sunset.”
units.literal: Take again Confucius’s words that one can reform, and Zigong’s saying that one may change; curb your speech in the crowd and save yourself a little in the record—this is what is called losing in the east corner and gaining in the mulberry west.

units.zh: 如此，令明主聞知，尚有冀也。
units.en: Do this, and if the wise sovereign learns of it, hope may yet remain.
units.literal: If you do so, the enlightened ruler may hear of it and there will still be hope.

units.zh: 僕東皋鄙人，入穴幸無銜窶，恥天下之士不爲執事道之，故披肝膽，示情素，君侯豈能鑒焉。」
units.en: I am a humble man of the eastern shore; though I live apart I am not ashamed to speak; I blush that no gentleman in the realm speaks frankly to you, and so I bare my inmost heart—will you not see it?”
units.literal: I am a rustic of the eastern marshes; though I have gone into hiding I am not yet ashamed to speak; I blush that gentlemen under heaven do not speak for you as they should, and so I lay bare my liver and show my heart—can you not discern it?”

units.zh: 太清元年，遷太子詹事，侍中如故。
units.en: In Taiqing 1, he was transferred to Crown Prince's Household Administrator, remaining Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
units.literal: In Taiqing 1, he was transferred to Crown Prince's Household Administrator, remaining Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.

units.zh: 二年，侯景襲京師，敬容自府移家臺內。
units.en: In the second year, when Hou Jing attacked the capital, Jingrong moved his household from his office into the imperial compound.
units.literal: In the second year, when Hou Jing attacked the capital, Jingrong moved his household from his office into the imperial compound.

units.zh: 初，景于渦陽退敗，未得審實，傳者乃云其將暴顯反，景身與衆並沒，朝廷以爲憂。
units.en: Earlier, when Jing had been defeated at Guoyang and no verified report had yet arrived, rumor said that his general Bao Xian had rebelled and that Jing himself and his troops had all perished, and the court was anxious over it.
units.literal: Earlier, when Jing had been defeated at Guoyang and no verified report had yet arrived, rumor said that his general Bao Xian had rebelled and that Jing himself and his troops had all perished, and the court was anxious over it.

units.zh: 敬容尋見東宮，太宗謂曰：「淮北始更有信，侯景定得身免，不如所傳。」
units.en: Jingrong soon had an audience in the Eastern Palace, and Taizong said to him, "News has only just come again from north of the Huai: Hou Jing certainly escaped alive, not as the rumors said."
units.literal: Jingrong soon had an audience in the Eastern Palace, and Taizong said to him, "News has only just come again from north of the Huai: Hou Jing certainly escaped alive, not as the rumors said."

units.zh: 敬容對曰：「得景遂死，深是朝廷之福。」
units.en: Jingrong replied, "If Jing had indeed died, it would be a great blessing for the court."
units.literal: Jingrong replied, "If Jing had indeed died, it would be a great blessing for the court."

units.zh: 太宗失色，問其故。
units.en: Taizong turned pale and asked the reason.
units.literal: Taizong turned pale and asked the reason.

units.zh: 敬容曰：「景翻覆叛臣，終當亂國。」
units.en: Jingrong said, "Jing is a treacherous rebel minister; in the end he will throw the state into disorder."
units.literal: Jingrong said, "Jing is a treacherous rebel minister; in the end he will throw the state into disorder."

units.zh: 是年，太宗頻於玄圃自講《老》《莊》二書，學士吳孜時寄詹事府，每日入聽。
units.en: That year Taizong often personally lectured on the Laozi and Zhuangzi at Xuanpu. The scholar Wu Zi was then attached to the Crown Prince's Household Administrator's office and entered every day to listen.
units.literal: That year Taizong often personally lectured on the Laozi and Zhuangzi at Xuanpu. The scholar Wu Zi was then attached to the Crown Prince's Household Administrator's office and entered every day to listen.

units.zh: 敬容謂孜曰：「昔晉代喪亂，頗由祖尚玄虛，胡賊殄覆中夏。
units.en: Jingrong said to Zi, "In the past, the disasters and disorder of the Jin were largely due to esteeming abstruse emptiness, and Hu bandits destroyed the central realm.
units.literal: Jingrong said to Zi, "In the past, the disasters and disorder of the Jin were largely due to esteeming abstruse emptiness, and Hu bandits destroyed the central realm.

units.zh: 今東宮復襲此，殆非人事，其將爲戎乎？」
units.en: Now the Eastern Palace is taking this up again. This scarcely seems like a human matter; is it about to become a barbarian calamity?"
units.literal: Now the Eastern Palace is taking this up again. This scarcely seems like a human matter; is it about to become a barbarian calamity?"

units.zh: 俄而侯景難作，其言有徵也。
units.en: Soon Hou Jing's calamity broke out, and his words were borne out.
units.literal: Soon Hou Jing's calamity broke out, and his words were borne out.

units.zh: 三年正月，敬容卒于圍內，詔贈仁威將軍，本官並如故。
units.en: In the first month of the third year, Jingrong died inside the siege. An edict posthumously granted him the title General of Benevolent Awe, with all his regular offices as before.
units.literal: In the first month of the third year, Jingrong died inside the siege. An edict posthumously granted him the title General of Benevolent Awe, with all his regular offices as before.

units.zh: 何氏自晉司空充、宋司空尚之，世奉佛法，並建立塔寺；
units.en: From Jin’s Grand Master He Chong and Song’s Grand Master He Shangzhi, the He family served Buddhism and raised pagodas and temples;
units.literal: The He clan from Jin Grand Master Chong and Song Grand Master Shangzhi onward all embraced Buddhism and each built pagodas and temples;

units.zh: 至敬容又舍宅東爲伽藍，趨勢者因助財造構，敬容並不拒，故此寺堂宇校飾，頗爲宏麗。
units.en: Jingrong too gave his eastern house for a monastery; flatterers supplied money to build it, and he did not refuse, so the shrine’s halls and ornaments grew very grand.
units.literal: Jingrong again donated his eastern residence as a monastery; men currying favor helped fund its construction, and Jingrong did not refuse, so the halls and adornments of this temple became quite magnificent.

units.zh: 時輕薄者因呼爲「衆造寺」焉。
units.en: Wits of the day nicknamed it the “Temple Built by the Crowd.”
units.literal: Men of frivolous wit therefore called it the “Everybody-built Temple.”

units.zh: 及敬容免職出宅，止有常用器物及囊衣而已，竟無餘財貨，時亦以此稱之。
units.en: When he was removed and quit his mansion, he took only ordinary goods and a bundle of clothes, with no wealth left—on this too the age praised him.
units.literal: When Jingrong was dismissed and left his house, he kept only everyday utensils and a bag of clothes, with no surplus wealth at all, and the age praised him for this as well.

units.zh: 子瑴，秘書丞，早卒。
units.en: His son Jiao, a secretariat aide, died early.
units.literal: His son Jiao was Secretariat Assistant and died young.

units.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：魏正始及晉之中朝，時俗尚於玄虛，貴爲放誕，尚書丞郎以上，簿領文案，不復經懷，皆成于令史。
units.en: Yao Cha, Chen Director of the Imperial Secretariat, said: From the Zhengshi reign through Jin’s middle courts the vogue favored abstruse talk and unrestrained conduct; secretariat directors and above no longer touched papers—everything fell to the clerks.
units.literal: Yao Cha, Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Chen, said: In the Zhengshi era and through the central courts of Jin, the fashion prized emptiness and mystery and honored reckless license; directors and gentlemen of the Secretariat and above no longer attended to documents and dossiers—all was left to the clerks.

units.zh: 逮乎江左，此道彌扇，惟卞壼以臺閤之務，頗欲綜理，阮孚謂之曰：「卿常無閒暇，不乃勞乎？」
units.en: Under the Eastern Jin the fashion spread further; only Bian Kun tried to manage secretariat business, and Ruan Fu told him: “You are never free—is that not toilsome?”
units.literal: By the time of the Eastern Jin this way spread still wider; only Bian Kun wished to put the secretariat’s affairs in order, and Ruan Fu said to him: “You are never at leisure—is it not laborious?”

units.zh: 宋世王敬弘身居端右，未嘗省牒，風流相尚，其流遂遠。
units.en: In Song, Wang Jinghong sat at the head yet never opened a file; elegance was admired, and the current ran deep.
units.literal: In the Song age Wang Hongjing held the chief seat yet never looked at a dispatch; men admired such elegance, and the stream flowed far.

units.zh: 望白署空，是稱清貴；
units.en: To stare at empty paper and leave the desk vacant was called refined dignity;
units.literal: To gaze at blank white and leave the office empty was called pure nobility;

units.zh: 恪勤匪懈，終滯鄙俗。
units.en: unflagging diligence in the end kept one among the coarse.
units.literal: diligence without slackness in the end stuck one among vulgar men.

units.zh: 是使朝經廢於上，職事隳於下。
units.en: So state discipline perished at the top and office work collapsed below.
units.literal: Thus court standards were abandoned above and official duties ruined below.

units.zh: 小人道長，抑此之由。
units.en: Petty ways flourished—and this is why.
units.literal: The petty man’s way grew long—this is where it came from.

units.zh: 嗚呼！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 傷風敗俗，曾莫之悟。
units.en: Manners were harmed and morals spoiled, and no one ever understood.
units.literal: Customs were injured and morals ruined, yet none ever woke to it.

units.zh: 永嘉不競，戎馬生郊，宜其然矣。
units.en: When Yongjia could no longer hold its own and war horses foaled by the city wall, it was only to be expected.
units.literal: The Yongjia era could not compete, and war horses were foaled in the suburbs—how fitting.

units.zh: 何國禮之識治，見譏薄俗，惜哉！
units.en: That He Guoli knew how to govern yet was scorned by shallow men—alas!
units.literal: He Guoli’s understanding of governance, seen in mockery by the vulgar—pity!

units.zh: 王彧、謝莊爲一雙，韜與何偃爲一雙。
units.en: Wang Yu and Xie Zhuang were paired; Tao and He Yan were paired.
units.literal: Wang Yu and Xie Zhuang were one pair; Tao and He Yan were one pair.

units.zh: 宋孝武選侍中四人，竝以風貌。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowu of Song picked four palace attendants, every one chosen for face and bearing.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song chose four palace attendants—all for their bearing and looks.

units.zh: 朱异、張綰議欲出擊之，高祖以問侃，侃曰：「不可。
units.en: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan urged a sortie; the emperor asked Kan, who said, “No.
units.literal: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan debated sallying out; the High Ancestor asked Kan, and Kan said: “No.

units.zh: 祖尚之，宋司空。
units.en: His grandfather Shangzhi had been minister of works under the Song.
units.literal: His grandfather Shangzhi was Song Minister of Works.

units.zh: 何戢字慧景，廬江灊人也。
units.en: He Ji, styled Huijing, came from Qian in Lujiang.
units.literal: He Ji, styled Huijing, was a native of Qian in Lujiang.

units.zh: 父偃，金紫光祿大夫，被遇於宋武。
units.en: His father Yan was golden-crown deputy grand master and had been favored by Song Wu.
units.literal: His father Yan was golden-crown deputy grand master and had won favor under Song Wu.

units.zh: 王敬弘
units.en: Wang Jinghong
units.literal: Wang Jinghong

units.zh: 王敬弘，琅邪臨沂人也。
units.en: Wang Jinghong was a native of Linyi in Langye.
units.literal: Wang Jinghong was a man of Linyi in Langye.

units.zh: 與高祖諱同，故稱字。
units.en: His given name matched the founding emperor's taboo name, so people called him by his courtesy name instead.
units.literal: His personal name was the same as the founding emperor's taboo name, so he was addressed by his courtesy name.

units.zh: 敬弘少有清尚，起家本國左常侍，衛軍參軍。
units.en: From youth Jinghong was known for pure and lofty character. He entered office as Left Attendant of his native commandery and as Army Aide to the Guard General.
units.literal: Jinghong in youth had pure and lofty aims; he began his career as Left Attendant of his native commandery and as Army Aide to the Guard General.

units.zh: 元嘉三年，為尚書僕射。
units.en: In the third year of Yuanjia he became Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
units.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he became Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 為天門太守。
units.en: He was appointed Administrator of Tianmen.
units.literal: He became Administrator of Tianmen.

units.zh: 尋徵為侍中。
units.en: Before long he was recalled to serve as Palace Attendant.
units.literal: Soon he was recalled as Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 嘗豫聽訟，上問以疑獄，敬弘不對。
units.en: Once when he sat in on a hearing, the emperor asked him about a difficult case, and Jinghong gave no answer.
units.literal: He once participated in hearing lawsuits; the emperor questioned him about a doubtful case, and Jinghong did not answer.

units.zh: 高祖西討司馬休之，敬弘奉使慰勞，通事令史潘尚於道疾病，敬弘單船送還都，存亡不測，有司奏免官，詔可。
units.en: When Emperor Gaozu marched west against Sima Xiuzhi, Jinghong was sent to comfort the army. Communications clerk Pan Shang fell ill on the road, and Jinghong sent him back to the capital alone by boat, with no certainty he would live. The authorities memorialized for Jinghong's dismissal, and the emperor approved.
units.literal: When the founding emperor campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi, Jinghong was sent on a mission to comfort the troops. The Communications Clerk Pan Shang fell ill on the road; Jinghong sent him back to the capital in a boat alone, his survival uncertain. The relevant offices memorialized to dismiss Jinghong from office, and the edict approved.

units.zh: 太祖即位，又以為散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，領江夏王師。
units.en: When Emperor Taizu came to the throne, Jinghong was again made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Jiangxia.
units.literal: When Emperor Taizu ascended the throne, Jinghong was again made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Jiangxia.

units.zh: 性恬靜，樂山水。
units.en: Quiet by nature, he loved mountains and rivers.
units.literal: His nature was tranquil and still; he delighted in mountains and streams.

units.zh: 敬弘之郡，玄時為荊州，遣信要令過。
units.en: When Jinghong set out for his post, Huan Xuan was governing Jingzhou and sent word asking him to come by on his way.
units.literal: When Jinghong went to his commandery, Xuan was then in Jingzhou and sent a messenger summoning him to pass through.

units.zh: 敬弘至巴陵，謂人曰：「靈寶見要，正當欲與其姊集聚耳，我不能為桓氏贅壻。」
units.en: At Baling Jinghong told those around him, "Lingbao wants me only so he can see his sister. I will not become a dependent son-in-law of the Huans."
units.literal: Jinghong reached Baling and said to others, "Lingbao has summoned me only because he wants to gather with his sister; I cannot become a son-in-law living under the Huan clan."

units.zh: 乃遣別船送妻往江陵。
units.en: He sent his wife onward to Jiangling in another boat.
units.literal: He then sent a separate boat to convey his wife to Jiangling.

units.zh: 妻在桓氏，彌年不迎。
units.en: His wife stayed with the Huans, and for a whole year he did not go to bring her home.
units.literal: His wife remained with the Huan family, and for a full year he did not go to fetch her.

units.zh: 山郡無事，恣其遊適，累日不回，意甚好之。
units.en: The mountain prefecture had little official business, and he roamed at will for days without returning, which pleased him greatly.
units.literal: In this mountain commandery there was little business; he gave free rein to roaming and pleasure, and for days on end did not return—he was exceedingly fond of it.

units.zh: 轉桓偉安西長史、南平太守。
units.en: He was transferred to serve as Chief Clerk on Huan Wei's Anxi staff and as Administrator of Nanping.
units.literal: He was transferred to serve as Chief Clerk on the Anxi staff under Huan Wei and as Administrator of Nanping.

units.zh: 去官，居作唐縣界。
units.en: He resigned his post and settled on the outskirts of Zuotang County.
units.literal: He left office and lived on the border of Zuotang County.

units.zh: 玄輔政及篡位，屢召不下。
units.en: When Huan Xuan held power and then seized the throne, he summoned Jinghong again and again, but Jinghong refused to take office.
units.literal: When Xuan assisted in government and usurped the throne, he repeatedly summoned Jinghong, who would not come down from retirement.

units.zh: 高祖以為車騎從事中郎，徐州治中從事史，征西將軍道規諮議參軍。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu made him Attendant Gentleman of the Household Cavalry, Registrar of Xuzhou, and Advisory Army Aide on the staff of Liu Daogui, General Who Conquers the West.
units.literal: The founding emperor appointed him Attendant Gentleman of the Household Cavalry, Registrar of Xuzhou, and Advisory Army Aide to the General Who Conquers the West, Liu Daogui.

units.zh: 嘗共酣飲致醉，敬弘因醉失禮，為外司所白，道規即更引還，重申初讌。
units.en: Once they drank together until drunk. Jinghong offended through drink and was reported by the supervisory office, but Daogui immediately had him brought back and held the feast again as before.
units.literal: They once drank together until drunk; Jinghong through drunkenness breached etiquette and was reported by the external office. Daogui at once summoned him back and renewed the original banquet.

units.zh: 召為中書侍郎，始攜家累自作唐還京邑。
units.en: Summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, he brought his family for the first time from Zuotang back to the capital.
units.literal: He was summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat and for the first time brought his household dependents from Zuotang back to the capital.

units.zh: 久之，轉黃門侍郎，不拜。
units.en: After a time he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, but he declined the post.
units.literal: After some time he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate but did not accept the appointment.

units.zh: 仍除太尉從事中郎，出為吳興太守。
units.en: He was next appointed Attendant of the Grand Marshal and then sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.
units.literal: He was then appointed Attendant of the Grand Marshal and sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.

units.zh: 舊居餘杭縣，悅是舉也。
units.en: He had long lived in Yuhang County and was delighted with the appointment.
units.literal: He had formerly lived in Yuhang County and was pleased with this appointment.

units.zh: 未及釋朝服，值赦復官。
units.en: He had not yet removed his court robes when an amnesty restored him to office.
units.literal: Before he had laid aside court dress, an amnesty came and he was restored to office.

units.zh: 宋國初建，為度支尚書，遷太常。
units.en: When the Song state was first established, he became Minister of Revenue and was then promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.
units.literal: When the Song state was first established, he became Minister of Revenue and was promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 高祖受命，補宣訓衛尉，加散騎常侍。
units.en: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, Jinghong was appointed Commandant of the Xuanxun Guard with the additional rank of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
units.literal: When the founding emperor received the Mandate, Jinghong was appointed Commandant of the Xuanxun Guard and given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

units.zh: 永初三年，轉吏部尚書，常侍如故。
units.en: In the third year of Yongchu he was transferred to Minister of the Civil Service while keeping his post as regular attendant.
units.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he was transferred to Minister of the Civil Service, retaining his regular attendant title as before.

units.zh: 敬弘每被除召，即便祗奉，既到宜退，旋復解官，高祖嘉其志，不苟違也。
units.en: Whenever Jinghong was appointed he dutifully accepted, but once he had taken up the post he thought it time to withdraw and soon resigned again. Emperor Gaozu admired this resolve and did not press him.
units.literal: Whenever Jinghong was appointed and summoned, he at once reverently accepted; once he had arrived it was fitting to withdraw, and he would promptly resign. The founding emperor praised his intent and did not lightly go against it.

units.zh: 復除廬陵王師，加散騎常侍，自陳無德，不可師範令王，固讓不拜。
units.en: He was again made Tutor to the Prince of Luling with the additional rank of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, but he declared himself without virtue and unfit to instruct a prince, firmly declined, and refused the appointment.
units.literal: He was again appointed Tutor to the Prince of Luling with the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry. He declared himself without virtue and unfit to instruct and model the prince, firmly declined, and did not accept.

units.zh: 又除祕書監，金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，本州中正，又不就。
units.en: He was next appointed Director of the Secretariat and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the additional posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Chief Rectifier of his native province, but again he did not accept.
units.literal: He was again appointed Director of the Secretariat, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and as Chief Rectifier of his native province, but again he did not take office.

units.zh: 關署文案，初不省讀。
units.en: He never bothered at first to read the paperwork from the offices under him.
units.literal: Regarding the documents of the offices under his charge, at first he did not examine and read them.

units.zh: 敬弘曰：「臣乃得訊牒讀之，政自不解。」
units.en: Jinghong said, "I have only just received and read the briefs, and I still do not understand the case."
units.literal: Jinghong said, "It is only now that I received and read the interrogation documents; I truly do not understand the case."

units.zh: 六年，遷尚書令，敬弘固讓，表求還東，上不能奪。
units.en: In the sixth year he was promoted to Director of the Imperial Secretariat, but Jinghong firmly declined and petitioned to return east, and the emperor could not change his mind.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Director of the Imperial Secretariat. Jinghong firmly declined and memorialized asking to return east; the emperor could not override him.

units.zh: 改授侍中、特進、左光祿大夫，給親信二十人。
units.en: He was instead made Palace Attendant, Special Advancement, and Left Grand Master of the Palace, with twenty personal retainers assigned to him.
units.literal: He was reassigned as Palace Attendant, Special Advancement, and Left Grand Master of the Palace, with twenty personal retainers granted.

units.zh: 讓侍中、特進，求減親信之半，不許。
units.en: He declined the posts of Palace Attendant and Special Advancement and asked that his retainers be cut in half, but the request was denied.
units.literal: He declined the posts of Palace Attendant and Special Advancement and asked that his personal retainers be reduced by half; this was not permitted.

units.zh: 及東歸，車駕幸冶亭餞送。
units.en: When he went home to the east, the emperor came in person to Ye Pavilion to see him off.
units.literal: When he returned east, the imperial carriage went in person to Ye Pavilion to give him a farewell feast.

units.zh: 敬弘妻，桓玄姊也。
units.en: Jinghong's wife was the elder sister of Huan Xuan.
units.literal: Jinghong's wife was Huan Xuan's elder sister.

units.zh: 累遷王府主簿、限外記室參軍、司徒主簿、太子中庶子、驃騎廬陵王府給事中郎、[3]中權何敬容府長史、給事黃門侍郎，坐事免。
units.en: He rose through chief clerk in a princely establishment, extra-quota recorder and staff aide, chief clerk in the Ministry over the Masses, junior mentor in the heir apparent's household, attendant gentleman in the establishment of the Prince of Luling as General of Agile Cavalry, [3] chief administrator in the establishment of He Jingrong of Central Authority, and Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then was dismissed for an offense.
units.literal: He rose through Chief Clerk in a princely establishment, Extra-Quota Recorder in a commandery staff, Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent, attendant gentleman in the establishment of the Prince of Luling, Grand General of Cavalry, Chief Clerk in the establishment of He Jingrong of Central Authority, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and was dismissed for an offense.

units.zh: 冰見表及書甚懼，以其絕遠，非所能制，遂與何充等奏聽皝稱燕王。
units.en: Yu Bing, terrified yet unable to coerce him from afar, joined He Chong in recommending that the court recognize the title of king of Yan.
units.literal: Bing seeing the memorial and letter was greatly afraid; because they were extremely distant, not what they could control; thereupon with He Chong and others memorialized to permit Huang to style King of Yan.

units.zh: 從叔昌珝謂曰：「求、點皆已高蹈，爾無宜復爾。
units.en: His uncle Chang Xu told him, "Qiu and Dian have both gone aloft—you need not follow.
units.literal: His uncle Chang Xu said, "Qiu and Dian have both ascended high—you need not do likewise.

units.zh: 何炯字士光，廬江灊人也。
units.en: He Jiong, styled Shiguang, was from Qian in Lujiang.
units.literal: He Jiong, styled Shiguang, was a man of Qian in Lujiang.

units.zh: 會有詔，士姓各舉四科，曇淨叔父慧斐舉以應孝行，高祖用爲海寧令。
units.en: When an edict bade each clan recommend four kinds of men, his uncle Huifei nominated him for filial conduct and Gaozu appointed him Haining magistrate.
units.literal: An edict came for gentry and commoners each to recommend four categories; his uncle Huifei recommended him for filial conduct and Gaozu made him Haining magistrate.

units.zh: 且君子出處，亦各一途。」
units.en: A gentleman's rise and retirement are each a proper way."
units.literal: Moreover the gentleman's going forth and staying have each their path."

units.zh: 世祖武皇帝情等布衣，寄深同氣。
units.en: Ancestor Emperor Wu treated him as an equal of the robe and bound him with shared blood.
units.literal: Ancestor Emperor Wu treated him as a commoner's equal and entrusted him with the bond of shared blood.

units.zh: 武皇大漸，實奉詔言。
units.en: When Emperor Wu lay dying, I truly received his charge in words.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu fell gravely ill, I truly received his charge in words.

units.zh: 時改選學職，以太尉江夏王義恭領國子祭酒，湛及侍中何攸之領博士。
units.en: Academic offices were reformed; Grand Marshal Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, became chancellor of the National University, while Zhan and Palace Attendant He Youzhi served as erudites.
units.literal: At the time academic offices were reformed; Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was made Chancellor of the National University, and Zhan together with Palace Attendant He Youzhi held the post of Erudite.

units.zh: 服闋，除太尉臨川王府外兵參軍、東宮領直。
units.en: After mourning he was named external military aide on the Prince of Linchuan's staff in the Grand Marshal's office and leader of direct service in the eastern palace.
units.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed External Military Aide on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan in the Grand Marshal's office and Leader of Direct Service in the Eastern Palace.

units.zh: 時中庶子謝嘏出守建安，於宣猷堂宴餞，並召時才賦詩，同用十五劇韻，愷詩先就，其辭又美。
units.en: At the time Junior Mentor Xie Xia was going out to guard Jian'an. At a farewell banquet in the Xuanyou Hall the talented men of the age were summoned to compose poems, all using the same fifteen rhyme categories. Kai's poem was finished first and its wording was also fine.
units.literal: At the time Junior Mentor Xie Xia was going out to guard Jian'an; at a farewell banquet in the Xuanyou Hall the talented men of the age were summoned to compose poems, all using the same fifteen rhyme categories; Kai's poem was finished first and its wording was also fine.

units.zh: 謝朏 弟子覽
units.en: Xie Fei; his nephew Lan
units.literal: Xie Fei; his nephew Lan

units.zh: 覽字景滌，朏弟綍之子也。
units.en: Lan, styled Jingdi, was the son of Fei's younger brother Fu.
units.literal: Lan, styled Jingdi, was the son of Fei's younger brother Fu.

units.zh: 選尚齊錢唐公主，拜駙馬都尉、秘書郎、太子舍人。
units.en: He was selected to marry the Princess of Qiantang of Qi and was appointed Imperial Son-in-law Commandant, Palace Library Gentleman, and attendant to the crown prince.
units.literal: He was selected to marry the Princess of Qiantang of Qi and was appointed Imperial Son-in-law Commandant, Palace Library Gentleman, and attendant to the crown prince.

units.zh: 天監元年，爲中書侍郎，掌吏部事，頃之卽真。
units.en: In Tianjian 1, Lan became Gentleman of the Secretariat and handled Personnel affairs; before long he took the office in his own right.
units.literal: In Tianjian 1, Lan became Gentleman of the Secretariat and handled Personnel affairs; before long he took the office in his own right.

units.zh: 尋遷吏部尚書。
units.en: Soon he became minister of personnel.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 頃之，敕掌東宮管記，遷明威將軍、新安太守。
units.en: Soon he was ordered to keep Eastern Palace records, promoted Bright Might general and Xin'an administrator.
units.literal: Shortly after, he was ordered to manage Eastern Palace records, promoted General of Bright Might and Administrator of Xin'an.

units.zh: 十二年春，出爲吳興太守。
units.en: In the twelfth year's spring he went out as Wuxing administrator.
units.literal: In spring of year twelve he went out as Administrator of Wuxing.

units.zh: 嘗侍座，受敕與侍中王暕爲詩答贈。
units.en: Once in attendance he was ordered, with Attendant Wang Jian, to compose answering verse for a gift exchange.
units.literal: Once while attending in his seat, he received an edict to compose an answering poem with Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Jian in reply to an exchange of gifts.

units.zh: 其文甚工。
units.en: The piece was finely wrought.
units.literal: His writing was very skilled.

units.zh: 子罕，早卒。
units.en: His son Han died early.
units.literal: His son Han died young.

units.zh: 九年夏，山賊吳承伯破宣城郡，餘黨散入新安，叛吏鮑敘等與合，攻沒黟、歙諸縣，進兵擊覽。
units.en: In the ninth year's summer, bandit Wu Chengbo broke Xuancheng; survivors fled into Xin'an; rebel clerks Bao Xu and others joined, took Yi and She, and marched on Lan.
units.literal: In summer of year nine, mountain bandit Wu Chengbo smashed Xuancheng commandery; remnants scattered into Xin'an; rebel clerk Bao Xu and others joined them, seized Yi and She counties, and advanced to attack Lan.

units.zh: 高祖爲大司馬，召補東閤祭酒，遷相國戶曹。
units.en: When Gaozu was Grand Marshal, he summoned Lan to fill the post of libationer of the Eastern Lodge; Lan was then transferred to the household section of the Chancellor of State.
units.literal: When Gaozu was Grand Marshal, he summoned Lan to fill the post of libationer of the Eastern Lodge; Lan was then transferred to the household section of the Chancellor of State.

units.zh: 覽遣郡丞周興嗣于錦沙立塢拒戰，不敵，遂棄郡奔會稽。
units.en: Lan sent assistant Zhou Xingsi to fortify Jinsha and fight; defeated, he abandoned the commandery and fled to Kuaiji.
units.literal: Lan sent Commandery Assistant Zhou Xingsi to build a stockade at Jinsha to resist; they were no match and he abandoned the commandery and fled to Kuaiji.

units.zh: 昔覽在新安頗聚斂，至是遂稱廉潔，時人方之王懷祖。
units.en: Once in Xin'an he had been grasping; now he was called incorrupt, and the age compared him to Wang Huainzu.
units.literal: Long ago in Xin'an Lan had greatly gathered wealth; now he was praised as pure and clean, and men compared him to Wang Huainzu.

units.zh: 卒于官，時年三十七。
units.en: He died in office at thirty-seven.
units.literal: He died in office at age thirty-seven.

units.zh: 詔贈中書令。
units.en: He was posthumously made palace library director.
units.literal: An edict posthumously made him Director of the Palace Library.

units.zh: 覽自祖至孫，三世居選部，當世以爲榮。
units.en: From grandfather through grandson, three generations held the personnel bureau—the age took it for honor.
units.literal: From grandfather to grandson, Lan's line held the selection bureau three generations—a glory of the age.

units.zh: 覽未到郡，睦之子弟來迎，覽逐去其船，杖吏爲通者。
units.en: Before Lan arrived, Muzhi's kin came to meet him; he drove off their boats and whipped the clerks who had let them through.
units.literal: Before Lan reached the commandery, Muzhi's kin came to welcome him; Lan drove off their boats and beat the clerks who had cleared the way for them.

units.zh: 自是睦之家杜門不出，不敢與公私關通。
units.en: After that Muzhi's clan stayed indoors and dared no public or private traffic.
units.literal: From then on Muzhi's household shut their doors and did not venture out, daring no private or official dealings.

units.zh: 郡境多劫，爲東道患，覽下車肅然，一境清謐。
units.en: Robbery was rife and troubled the eastern roads; when Lan took office the whole district grew orderly and still.
units.literal: The commandery had many robbers and was a scourge on the eastern route; when Lan took his carriage down the district grew stern and the whole region grew quiet.

units.zh: 覽爲人美風神，善辭令，高祖深器之。
units.en: Lan had a handsome presence and gift for speech; the Founding Emperor prized him greatly.
units.literal: Lan was a man of fine bearing and spirit, skilled in eloquence; Gaozu deeply valued him.

units.zh: 覽頗樂酒，因醼席與散騎常侍蕭琛辭相詆毀，爲有司所奏。
units.en: Lan loved wine; at a feast he and Regular Attendant Xiao Chen traded insults, and the authorities memorialized against them.
units.literal: Lan was quite fond of wine; at a banquet with Regular Attendant of the Writes-on-the-Fast Xiao Chen they exchanged abusive words and were reported by the authorities.

units.zh: 高祖以覽年少不直，出爲中權長史。
units.en: The Emperor, holding Lan young and not upright, sent him out as Central Guards chief clerk.
units.literal: Gaozu, because Lan was young and not straightforward, sent him out as Chief Clerk of the Central Guards.

units.zh: 臺軍平山寇，覽復還郡，左遷司徒諮議參軍、仁威長史、行南徐州事，五兵尚書。
units.en: When the army pacified the bandits, Lan returned; then he was demoted to Masters of Works adviser, Humaneness and Might chief clerk, acting South Xuzhou, and Five Armaments minister.
units.literal: When court troops pacified the mountain raiders, Lan returned to the commandery, then was demoted to Adviser of the Minister of the Masters of Works, Chief Clerk of Humaneness and Might, acting South Xuzhou affairs, and Minister of the Five Armaments.

units.zh: 初，齊明帝及覽父綍、東海徐孝嗣，並爲吳興，號稱名守，覽皆欲過之！
units.en: Once Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Fu, and Donghai's Xu Xiaosi had all ruled Wuxing as famed administrators—Lan meant to outdo them all!
units.literal: Earlier Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Fu, and Xu Xiaosi of Donghai had all governed Wuxing and been called famed administrators—Lan wished to surpass them all!

units.zh: 覽終能善政，君子韙之。
units.en: Lan could govern well to the end; gentlemen praised it.
units.literal: Lan in the end could govern well; gentlemen approved him.

units.zh: 昔王允秉誠，卞壼峻節，均風往德，歸茂先軌。
units.en: In former times Wang Yun held fast to sincerity and Bian Kun had stern integrity. Both matched the virtue of the past and return glory to the former track.
units.literal: In former times Wang Yun held fast to sincerity and Bian Huai had stern integrity; both matched the virtue of the past and return glory to the former track.
